findings.where: How to check this file, README.env-vars.md:1139-1140
findings.problem: The sentence "At the baseline commit the commands print no name." is false. The commands print one name, `SELF_DIR`. `SELF_DIR` is a shell variable, not an environment variable. The file does not hold the name in backticks, so the check reports it as missing.
findings.evidence: I ran the code block of README.env-vars.md:1119-1136 unchanged from the root of the checkout (branch jhan-env-vars-doc, HEAD 7eddde7895 plus the three staged files). Output: one line, "SELF_DIR". Exit status 0. Both temporary files were removed. Source of the name: perfetto/launcher-common:7 `: "${SELF_DIR:?launcher-common must be sourced with SELF_DIR set}"`. perfetto/tronperf:3 and perfetto/wrapper:3 assign `SELF_DIR=$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")` before they source that file. No file exports the name. A copy of the document with `SELF_DIR` added in backticks made the same commands print nothing.
findings.fix:
Replace lines 1139-1140 with:

The check treats every name in backticks in this file as known.

The shell pattern also matches a shell variable that is not an environment
variable. `SELF_DIR` is such a name. The scripts `perfetto/tronperf` and
`perfetto/wrapper` assign it, and then `perfetto/launcher-common` tests it.
This paragraph holds the name in backticks, so the commands do not print it.

At the baseline commit the commands print no name.

findings.where: Rules for developers, rule 2, README.env-vars.md:105
findings.problem: The rule does not say how to compare `_` with letters, or two names that differ only in case. All 48 variable tables are sorted when the names are compared in lower case (ASCII order). With the usual shell check `LC_ALL=C sort -f`, which compares in upper case, 4 tables are not sorted: 5.4, 6.5, 7.4 and 7.6. A developer who checks with `sort -f` will "fix" rows that are in the intended order.
findings.evidence: Script over all 405 rows: lower-case comparison finds 0 tables out of order. `LC_ALL=C sort -f` moves these rows: `__NIX_USERNAME` and `CMAKE_C_COMPILER` / `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` (5.4, lines 791-794), `SLICE_REFRESH_RUN_URL` / `SLICE_REFRESH_RUNNER_CLASS` (6.5, lines 897-898), `PY_COLORS` / `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` (7.4, lines 1032-1033), `http_proxy` / `HTTPS_PROXY` (7.6, lines 1065-1066). In 7.6 the upper-case name of each pair comes first (lines 1062-1069).
findings.fix:
2. Keep the rows of each table sorted by name. Compare the names in lower
   case, in ASCII order: a digit comes before `_`, and `_` comes before a
   letter. When two names differ only in case, put the upper-case name first.

findings.where: How to set a variable > A test, README.env-vars.md:353-358
findings.problem: The sentence "`bin/slice` sets `TRON_LOG_DIR`, `SYSTEM_CONFIG` and `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH` for each test that it starts" is broader than the code. It is true for `bin/slice run`. `bin/slice bench` starts each test with `SYSTEM_CONFIG` only. The next bullet then speaks of "the three values that `bin/slice` sets". The statement that a `bin/slice` value wins over a declared CTest value is true.
findings.evidence: bin/slice:4696-4704 (`cmd_run`) and bin/slice:3461-3467 (`_run_unbenched_batch`) pass SYSTEM_CONFIG, TRON_LOG_DIR and RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH to `make_test_env`. bin/slice:1904-1909 (`benchmark_test`, called from `_cmd_bench` at line 2479) passes only SYSTEM_CONFIG. Precedence: bin/slice:1700-1704 and 1729 apply the CTest ENVIRONMENT entries first and the Slice values last (`managed.update(slice_overrides)`). t/CMakeLists.txt:866 declares `SYSTEM_CONFIG=--instance 0,4` for one test. doc/slice.md:437-438 describes the three variables for `slice run` only.
findings.fix:
- `bin/slice run` sets `TRON_LOG_DIR`, `SYSTEM_CONFIG` and `RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH`
  for each test that it starts. `bin/slice bench` sets only `SYSTEM_CONFIG`.
  See [doc/slice.md](doc/slice.md).
- A test can declare more variables in its `ENVIRONMENT` property in
  `t/CMakeLists.txt`. CTest sets them, and `bin/slice` sets them too. A value
  that `bin/slice` sets wins over a declared value of the same name.

findings.where: How to set a variable > A program that a person starts, README.env-vars.md:332-340
findings.problem: Two statements about Dice do not match `bin/dice`. (1) "Dice changes that environment in three ways" is narrower than the code. The daemon also sets `DICE_LABEL` when the submission has a label, and it fills in `PATH`, `USER`, `LOGNAME` and `HOME` when the submitted environment lacks them. (2) "the Dice service variables of section 2.4" is broader than the code and uses a term that the file does not define. Section 2.4 has 11 rows. The daemon removes 8 of them. It keeps `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SHADOW_SHARED`, `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_RUNNER` and `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SPAWN_OK`. The statement about `DICE_DISABLE` and the statement about `--instance` in `SYSTEM_CONFIG` are true.
findings.evidence: bin/dice:3629-3645 removes DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH, DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG, DICE_RUNTIME_DIR, DICE_SOCKET_PATH, DICE_STATE_PATH, DICE_LOG_PATH, DICE_LOCK_PATH, DICE_LOG_DIR and DICE_DISABLE, on a shared host and only when no test host configuration is active. bin/dice:3646-3651 sets defaults for PATH, USER, LOGNAME and HOME. bin/dice:3656-3661 sets DICE_SLOTS, DICE_DAEMON_CHILD, DICE_GRANT_ID and DICE_GRANT_TOKEN. bin/dice:3683-3684 sets DICE_LABEL. bin/dice:3662-3677 with `_merge_system_config` (bin/dice:1084-1124) replaces `--instance` only when the granted slots map to an instance, and keeps the other tokens. The row of `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_SHADOW_SHARED` (README.env-vars.md:549) says that the daemon does not remove it.
findings.fix:
Replace lines 332-340 with:

On a shared host, Dice starts the program with the environment of the person
who submitted the work. Dice changes that environment in these ways:

- It adds the grant variables of section 2.2.
- It sets `DICE_LABEL` when the submission has a label.
- It sets `PATH` when the submitted environment lacks it. It does the same for
  `USER`, `LOGNAME` and `HOME`, from the password database entry of the
  submitter.
- It removes `DICE_DISABLE` and these variables of section 2.4:
  `DICE_ALLOW_TEST_HOST_CONFIG`, `DICE_LOCK_PATH`, `DICE_LOG_DIR`,
  `DICE_LOG_PATH`, `DICE_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DICE_SOCKET_PATH`, `DICE_STATE_PATH`
  and `DICE_TEST_HOST_CONFIG_PATH`. It keeps the other variables of that
  section.
- When the grant has the form of an `--instance` share, it takes the
  `--instance` choice in `SYSTEM_CONFIG` from the grant, not from the
  submitted value.

findings.where: Rules for developers, rule 1, second bullet, README.env-vars.md:97-99
findings.problem: The exception "a name that changes how `rinzler` or `runtron` behaves" is wider than the layout. `PATH` also changes how they behave, by its own row, and its row is in section 7.1. The layout follows a narrower rule: a library inside the process reads the name.
findings.evidence: Section 1 rows that other software defines and that no Tron source reads: `TZ` (C library), `SPDLOG_LEVEL` (spdlog), `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` (crate `openai-harmony`), `PERFETTO_PRODUCER_SOCK_NAME` (Perfetto SDK). Row `PATH` (README.env-vars.md:926): "For the Python tokenizer, `rinzler` and `runtron` start the script `bin/tokenize_py` through a shell. That script finds `python3` through `PATH`."
findings.fix:
- A name that other software defines goes in section 7. The exception is a
     name that a library inside `rinzler` or `runtron` reads, such as `TZ`.
     That name goes in section 1. A name that only a child process reads, such
     as `PATH`, stays in section 7.

findings.where: How to set a variable > A `rinzler` service instance, tron-host paragraph, README.env-vars.md:317-322
findings.problem: The paragraph is true, but it does not say which value wins. The drop-in sets its two variables with `Environment=` lines. So a value of the same name in one of the two files still wins. This follows from the rule that the section already states at lines 277-278.
